public_rationale: Contemporary independent coding tests found failures in the April 9 Turbo release. A dated primary user report also identified incorrect factual self-description and supplied reproduction code. Together they support the limited observation that errors persisted. They do not establish how often ordinary users encountered hallucinations or validate every detail of the unseen Libin example.
limitations: The coding test measures task completion, not hallucination frequency.
The factual-error evidence is a user report with reproduction instructions, not independent replication.
Persistence does not establish worsening performance or an inability to improve.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that factual mistakes and plainly unsuccessful responses persisted, including in the newly released GPT-4 Turbo. It does not claim that accuracy had never improved.
Interpret GPT-Turbo as gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 and assess its release through the April 13 post.
The claim supplies no error-rate threshold. Documented failures can establish persistence without establishing their prevalence.
criteria.support_condition: Dated tests or reproducible reports identify continuing factual mistakes and task failures in the April GPT-4 Turbo release.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence establishes that the alleged failures were misattributed or erroneous and that the named release had eliminated the relevant problems across its intended uses. Isolated successful answers are insufficient.
